;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings]]
**A series of explosions at churches and hotels in four cities in [[Sri Lanka]], including the nation's commercial capital and largest city  [[Colombo]], kills at least 359 people and wounds around 500 others. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] has since claimed responsibility for the attacks. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-48008073 (BBC News)] 
**The Sri Lankan government temporarily [[Censorship in South Asia#Sri Lanka|blocks access]] to all [[social media]] platforms to stop the spread of "false media reports" about the attacks.  [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2019/04/21/sri-lankan-government-blocks-social-media-imposes-curfew-following-deadly-blasts/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] has stated that several United States citizens were killed in the attacks and Sri Lanka's Foreign Ministry officials have stated that at least five of the victims were of British nationality. [https://www.cnn.com/asia/live-news/sri-lanka-easter-sunday-explosions-dle-intl/h_7cf075d83c893b55b334e94892ffb15c (CNN)]
**[[Pope Francis]] speaks words of solidarity to the Christian community of Sri Lanka, lamenting that the attacks have wrought grief and sorrow. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2019-04/pope-francis-laments-sri-lanka-attacks-on-easter.html (Vatican News)]
*Four attackers are killed in a failed attack on a police station in [[Zulfi]], [[Saudi Arabia]]. The attackers had machine guns, bombs, and petrol bombs. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/04/killed-foiled-attack-saudi-police-station-reports-190421101113605.html (Al Jazeera)]
*Suspected jihadist militants attack a [[Military of Mali|Malian military]] base in the town of [[Guiré]], [[Koulikoro Region]], killing ten soldiers. [https://www.dw.com/en/mali-soldiers-killed-in-suspected-jihadist-attack/a-48422811 (Deutsche Welle)]

;Disasters and accidents
*28 people are killed and two others are missing after a [[landslide]] in the municipality of [[Rosas, Cauca|Rosas]], in southwestern [[Colombia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-48021710 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Ukrainian presidential election]]
**According to exit polls, comedian  [[Volodymyr Zelensky]] wins Ukraine's presidential run-off election over incumbent [[President of Ukraine|President]] [[Petro Poroshenko]] with more than 70 percent of the votes. Poroshenko concedes defeat. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ukraine-election/comedian-zelenskiy-wins-ukrainian-presidential-race-by-landslide-exit-poll-idUSKCN1RX01N (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48007487 (BBC News)] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-presidential-election-second-round-1.5105896 (CBC)]
*[[2019 North Macedonian presidential election]]
**[[North Macedonia|Macedonia]]ns go to the polls to elect the next [[President of North Macedonia]] in an election dominated by divisions over the [[Prespa agreement]], which resolved the [[Macedonia naming dispute|naming dispute]] between North Macedonia and [[Greece]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-north-macedonia-election/macedonians-vote-in-election-dominated-by-splits-over-name-change-idUSKCN1RX008 (Reuters)]
